description: Explicitly recover a recurring error schedule at expected_revision with a nonempty reason, after a separate destination rebind if needed. One CAS transaction sets scheduled, clears error and appends history/epoch while preserving actions and cadence. It reconciles exactly one cron job without immediate firing, preserving existing timing. activation_status=pending and effective=false disclose unavailable activation; startup restore or an explicit retry reconciles it. An already-scheduled current revision returns already_scheduled without extra mutation/history. Stale revisions and terminal/one-time rows cannot recover.
embedding_description: Explicitly recover an errored recurring schedule at its current revision, preserving action text and cadence. Record the transition and ensure exactly one runtime cron job. Report pending activation honestly; repeated current-revision recovery is idempotent. Rebind destinations separately.

result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Show completeness, holder observation, revision and activation advisories explicitly. A registered route is an observation, not a delivery guarantee.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Read current revision before a mutation. Recovery is a separate explicit action. Pre-boundary queued work is unchanged.

error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: A stale revision or invalid lifecycle transition is a data-integrity refusal; unavailable observations are advisories.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Read the current owner projection and history, then make an explicit correction with its current revision. Do not recreate a schedule to bypass a stale revision.
